extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using a text-to-image methodology with Stable Diffusion. The dataset is created by constructing texture-specific prompts combining artistically-informed descriptors and applying a three-stage refinement process (frequency filtering, patch variance filtering, and CLIP score filtering) to ensure high quality, diversity, and prompt alignment.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel (University of Wisconsin-Madison)
extraction.citeAs: Hoak, B. and McDaniel, P. On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation. arXiv:2409.10297v3 [cs.CV], 9 May 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Texture images were generated using Stable Diffusion text-to-image models with texture-specific prompts. Prompts were constructed by combining descriptors across categories (texture, artistic, spatial, enhancer, color) resulting in 96,768 unique prompts. Five images were generated per prompt, yielding 483,840 images before refinement. Images flagged as NSFW by the safety filter were excluded from the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Up to 60% of initially generated images were flagged as NSFW by the Stable Diffusion safety filter and excluded from the final dataset. Images flagged as NSFW were regenerated to ensure a consistent number of images per prompt.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images generated by the Stable Diffusion model using 96,768 unique texture-specific prompts, producing 483,840 images before refinement. The Stable Diffusion model was accessed via HuggingFace.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Images flagged as NSFW by the Stable Diffusion safety filter were regenerated to ensure a consistent number of non-flagged images per prompt.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts were structured by combining one word from each descriptor category (artistic, spatial, color enhancer, color, texture) in standard English adjective order, producing 96,768 unique prompts. Five images were generated per prompt using Stable Diffusion.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied: (1) Frequency filtering - retaining the top 80% of images with the highest frequency cutoff values (fc) per texture class to remove object-like images; (2) Patch variance filtering - dividing images into 50x50 pixel non-overlapping patches, computing variance of mean patch intensities, and removing the bottom 20% of images with lowest patch variance per texture class to eliminate homogeneous images; (3) CLIP score filtering - removing the bottom 20% of images with the lowest CLIP scores per texture class to ensure prompt alignment. After refinement, 246,285 images remained.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation was conducted with 9 participants, each shown 100 images in random order. For each image, participants rated (1) overall image quality and (2) how well the image represents the provided descriptor, both on a scale of 1 to 5. Images were selected randomly from the dataset before the refinement stage, with no duplicate images between or within participant sets, evaluating 900 unique images total.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Mean quality and representativeness scores were computed across images at each stage of the refinement process. CLIP scores were validated against human representative scores, showing strong alignment. The refinement process yielded a 3.4% increase in quality and a 4.5% increase in representativeness overall. Patch Variance refinement contributed most to quality improvement, while CLIP filtering contributed most to representativeness improvement.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 ratings per image (quality and representativeness), each from 1 annotator (images were not duplicated across participants)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion (image generation), CLIP scores (cosine similarity between text and image embeddings for prompt alignment filtering), Inception model (Inception scores for quality and diversity evaluation), FID scores (Fréchet Inception Distance for realism evaluation), Fourier transform (frequency analysis for object removal filtering)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset is available for download at https://zenodo.org/records/15359142. The methodology is described as extensible. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables research into texture bias in machine learning models, which has implications for model trustworthiness, interpretability, and robustness. The dataset has been used to develop the Texture Object Association Values (TAV) metric, which found that texture type can affect model accuracy by up to 66% and confidence by up to 40%, and that 90% of natural adversarial examples contained misaligned texture information.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Variation in quality across texture classes was observed, with textures that commonly appear in objects (e.g., hairy, flaky) tending to have better Inception and FID scores, while more structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted) tended to have worse scores. Some descriptor word pairs are more compatible than others, influencing image quality. The NSFW safety filter disproportionately flagged certain texture classes (e.g., nearly 100% of prompts containing 'paisley' produced at least one flagged image).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is generated synthetically using Stable Diffusion and may not fully capture all properties of real textures. The Stable Diffusion model is not explicitly designed to create textures, so object-like images may arise. Structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted) tend to have lower quality scores. Some descriptor combinations yield lower quality images (e.g., 'muted' and 'earthy' paired with subtle textures). Inception and FID metrics were originally designed for object-based datasets and may not fully capture texture-specific quality.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Texture-based research including: measuring texture bias in machine learning models, constructing texture-object associations, studying model interpretability, creating adversarial examples, training and evaluating computer vision models on texture data, and supporting large-scale texture analysis. The dataset has been used as the basis for the Texture Object Association Values (TAV) metric.
